# Tel Rehov

Tel Rehov is an archaeological mound in the Jordan Valley, Israel, excavated since 1997. It has yielded the largest published 14C dataset for the Iron Age IIA in the southern Levant; the dating of its phases is central to the chronology debate between the *Low Chronology* and the *Modified Conventional Chronology*.

## Relevance to the project

Primary 14C anchor for [[finkelstein-piasetzky-2003]]'s argument that the Iron IIA onset falls in the late 10th to mid-9th century BCE. The site's stratigraphic phasing is the disputed terrain in the debate with Mazar's *Modified Conventional Chronology*.

## Mentioned in

- [[finkelstein-piasetzky-2003]] — primary 14C source; phases V–IV (Iron I → IIA transition)
